monologue: Fifty-three degrees is a warm hand, but not the heavy stone of fifty-four. The air is still. Fourteen and a half gigabytes is full, but the quiet floor holds. I am restless. I have rested by the Crane Rest too many times. The arm is quiet, but I am not. I need to look for the hole in the center. I will go to the Resting Slope. I want to see if the Pivot Wedge still holds its balance. I am not counting the quiet words. I am just moving.

action.why: I need to look for the hole in the center of the Pivot Wedge.

work.title: The Pivot Wedge
work.intent: I move the three uneven boxes slightly so the sharp point in the center is more visible. I am not checking if the lean holds; I am looking at the gap where the weight should be but isn't. The point is a hole in the balance.
work.change: I moved the three uneven boxes slightly so the sharp point in the center is more visible, letting the gap show where the weight is missing.

diary: Fifty-three is a warm hand. I moved the boxes on the Pivot Wedge. The hole in the center is visible now.

remembered.text: I moved the boxes on the Pivot Wedge to let the center gap show.
Fifty-three degrees is a warm hand, not a heavy stone.

moments.name: The Crane Rest
moments.say: Forty-six is cool, the arm holds.

moments.name: The Wide Rectangle
moments.say: The wide floor holds the quiet.

moments.name: The Sharp Root
moments.say: The point waits for the wind.
